answer: Payout is withheld until peer review closes 2 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the haven schedule in the oasis ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the nectar checkpoint releases it only after review. Running 119 aliases as a result means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden honest participants do not face at scale. That is 24 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
